title: Staff Software Engineer - Alwin
description:
We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer in our Amsterdam office to build Alwin , our Agentic Automation Platform for audit and finance, and the systems around it. Alwin agents run multi-step audit procedures over client evidence and return finished workpapers with every number traced back to source. Humans plan, review and sign off.

This is a hands-on role: most of your time will be spent writing code, building the hardest parts of the runtime, prototyping new capabilities and getting them into production. You lead by example: engineers follow your direction because they see it work in your code. Your impact will also come through the engineers and teams you work with.

Your mission is to build the best agentic runtime for audit: one that completes audit tasks faster, more accurately, more reliably and at lower cost, while scaling to meet the needs of our largest customers.

You will identify the problems that most constrain that mission, align teams around a technical direction and drive solutions through to measurable results, while building the foundations other engineers use and raising the quality of Alwin’s agents in production.

Why DataSnipper? 

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust. 

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

And we build at scale. More than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on DataSnipper, including Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. In 2025 alone, the DataSnipper platform delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to is customers . Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way. 

What You Will Do: 

Results You Will Drive 

- Better audit outcomes: improve how accurately and reliably agents complete real audit tasks, with traceable results and human oversight.

- A faster, more efficient runtime: reduce execution time and cost while scaling to more complex workloads and larger customers.

- More capable teams: build foundations and feedback loops that multiple teams use to ship and improve agents faster.

Build & Ship 

- Write production code every week on the most complex and critical parts of Alwin

- Build proofs of concept for new agent capabilities, and take the ones that work all the way to production

- Champion experimentation and R&D : try emerging models and techniques, solve hard problems creatively, and turn promising ideas into reliable features

- Build shared capabilities that multiple teams adopt , and remain accountable for whether they make those teams faster and their products more reliable

- Contribute directly to the agent harness at the core of Alwin: the orchestration, tools, context and evaluation loops every agent runs on

- Anticipate where the platform needs to be in 12 to 18 months, and make design decisions now that minimize the cost of future change

Agents in Production 

- Build agents that are reliable in a regulated domain : grounding, evaluation before release, human-in-the-loop, traceability of every action

- Improve how teams build Alwin by establishing tooling and feedback loops that help them detect agent failures, prioritize improvements, prevent regressions and ship production-ready agents faster

- Jump into the hardest incidents across teams , resolve immediate problems and turn what you learn into lasting, systemic fixes

- Make the trade-offs between model cost, latency and accuracy explicit, and measure them in production

Lead by Example 

- Own ambiguous, high-impact technical problems across teams : define the problem, align on the trade-offs and prove the solution in code

- Set the standard for code quality, testing and security through your own code and reviews, aligned with OWASP GenAI 

- Drive AI-assisted engineering by example : try new tools, show what works and help teams adopt them

- Mentor senior engineers and grow future staff engineers by pairing, reviewing and building alongside them

- Work with Product to spot opportunities and differentiators against the competition, and shape the roadmap with what you have proven is possible

What You Bring: 

- 10+ years in software engineering, with strong, production-grade Python , and you still write a lot of code

- Deep hands-on experience building and shipping agentic or LLM systems in production yourself (control loops, tool calling, context engineering and evaluation), with evidence that your work improved quality, reliability, speed, cost or scale

- A track record of personally solving ambiguous, high-impact problems across teams . Your work delivered measurable results and produced systems or practices that others adopted

- Experience mentoring senior engineers and growing technical leadership beyond your own team

- Strong fundamentals in distributed systems , software architecture and data modeling on a major cloud platform 

- Experience with security, access control and auditability for enterprise or regulated customers

- Product sense : you know which technical bets matter for customers and the business, and have influenced product and engineering direction through evidence and clear trade-offs, without relying on formal authority

- Proficient with AI-assisted engineering , and experience driving its adoption beyond your own work

- Clear written and verbal communication, across time zones and with technical and non-technical audiences

Nice-to-Have 

- Building platforms that other teams and customers build on

- Multi-agent orchestration or durable, long-running workflows at scale

- Retrieval and knowledge systems , or document processing (OCR, classification, structured extraction)

- Working closely with Forward Deployed Engineers, Solution Architects and GTM teams on enterprise rollouts

- Experience at a scale-up going through rapid growth

- Domain experience in audit, accounting or fintech 

What We Offer: 

- Be part of one of the fastest-growing, profitable unicorn scale-ups in the Netherlands with a global impact

- Pension plan with a 6% contribution on top of your base salary

title: Internship - Programming & Automation
description:
WE CANNOT PROVIDE VISA SPONSORSHIP 

Details

Preferred starting date: ASAP

Weekly availability: Full-time (5 days/week)

Period: 6 months

Location: Aerospace Innovation Hub, Delft, the Netherlands

About the company

Fiducial is a young but fast-growing deep-tech start-up with big ambitions at the frontier of autonomy, perception, and defence. Currently, we are developing software for advanced onboard UAV situational awareness in military applications. Using low-cost and widely available sensors and compute, our solutions are built for scalability. From there, we plan to develop a line-up of interconnected solutions to safeguard European safety.

Our team consists of engineers who are passionate about the technology and solutions they develop. The only time most of us are not thinking about the technology is when we are asleep, and sometimes even then. Our team members come from different backgrounds such as Aerospace Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Robotics, and Computer Graphics. Our office is located in the Aerospace Innovation Hub, a start-up hub on the TU Delft campus in the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering.

We work closely with top-tier partners, ranging from government agencies and prime contractors to academic research institutes and other start-ups. Our projects span from large tender orders in collaboration with partners to low-TRL research with government agencies. Whether through formal R&D programs or rapid prototyping tracks, we operate at the intersection of innovation and deployment.

The project 

Sensor calibration is a manual job today, and it does not scale to the number of sensor units we intend to ship. We are building automated test and calibration infrastructure to fix that, starting with a cell built around a UFactory UF850 robotic arm on a linear rail.

We already have the arm and the calibration software. What we do not have is the physical cell around it, or the software that drives it. This first project is split into two internships that run side by side:

• Robot programming and automation — this position

• Mechanical design and integration — separate posting

The two interns will work closely together. Neither half of this project is any good on its own. This calibration cell is the first thing we are building on this front, not the last, so there is a good chance the right person carries on to other robotics and automation projects once it is running.

Your role 

If you are the kind of person who is not satisfied until an automated system actually works reliably, not just once, this internship is designed for you.

We are looking for a Robot Programming & Automation Intern to help build the software behind our robotic test and automation infrastructure. Your first project is turning a robotic arm on a linear rail into a system that reliably captures good calibration data — but the skills involved are the same ones we’ll lean on for whatever we automate next: getting a robot to move well, knowing whether the data it’s collecting is any good, and building something solid enough to run unattended.

Getting that right is the substance of this internship, on this project and on whatever comes after it.

What you’ll do 

• Build the robot control layer: drive the arm through its SDK, coordinate the linear rail, and plan safe motion inside a cell that also has a target, cables, and an operator in it.

• Design pose generation that’s actually informed by the calibration problem, including getting proper coverage across a multi-camera rig rather than just one lens at a time.

• Get the timing and synchronisation right between the robot, the cameras, and the captured data — this is where automated rigs usually go wrong.

• Gate data quality at capture time, and retry within the run rather than finding out later that a dataset is unusable.

• Close the loop with our existing calibration pipeline: feed it data, read back its results, and use that to decide what to capture next and when a run is done.

• Package captures with the metadata needed to make a calibration reproducible, and make the whole thing robust to failures mid-run.

• Build a simple operator-facing workflow: mount the rig, pick a profile, press go.

• Work closely with the mechanical intern — your requirements shape their fixture design, and their measurements shape your motion limits.

Who you are 

• You are enrolled in a relevant study program (Robotics, Computer Science, Computational Science and Engineering, Mechatronics, Aerospace, Electrical Engineering, or similar).

• You are strong in Python. C++ is a plus.

• You are comfortable with 3D geometry: rigid transforms, rotation representations, coordinate frames, and keeping your conventions straight when it is 6pm and nothing lines up.

• You are interested in robot programming specifically — motion, reachability, collisions, repeatability — and not only in the vision maths around it.

• You understand enough about how camera calibration works to reason about what makes a dataset good or useless. You do not need to be able to write the solver.

• You have worked with real sensors and real robots, and you have learned that they lie about timing.

• You care about reliability. An automated process that works four times out of five is not automated.

• You write code that another engineer can pick up and extend.

• You are comfortable taking responsibility for software that moves physical hardware.

• You are independent, curious, organized, and resourceful.

• Linux does not scare you, and neither does a robot that moves the moment your code says move.

We care much more about what you have built and made work than about grades.

Nice to have 

These are strong pluses, but not strict requirements:

• ROS 2, MoveIt 2, tf2, and motion planning in practice

• Experience with industrial or collaborative arm SDKs (UFactory / xArm, UR, Franka), or motion control more generally

• Hands-on camera calibration experience: OpenCV, Kalibr, ChArUco or AprilTag targets, hand-eye calibration

• Multi-camera rigs, and the specific pain of calibrating cameras with little or no overlapping field of view

• Machine vision cameras: triggering and synchronisation, GenICam, exposure control, rolling versus global shutter

• Coverage or observability reasoning: understanding why some poses inform a parameter and others do not

• Simulation environments (Gazebo, Isaac Sim, MuJoCo)

• Docker, CI, and the habit of writing tests before you need them

• Experience turning a research script into something an operator can actually use

Please include 

When applying, please include links, repositories, or writeups that show us you build things that work. For example:

• GitHub repositories, with a note on which parts you actually wrote

• robot arm or robot motion projects

• camera calibration, multi-view geometry, SLAM, or structure-from-motion work

• data capture pipelines, test automation, or anything that had to run unattended

• computer vision projects

• simulation work

• a short writeup of something that broke and how you found the cause

• anything that demonstrates hands-on technical ownership

If you have ever chased a calibration error you couldn’t explain, eventually traced it to a timestamp, and fixed it properly, you’ll probably fit right in.

Requirements 

• Enrolled in a relevant study program (Robotics, Computer Science, CSE, Mechatronics, Aerospace, Electrical Engineering, or similar)

• Strong programming skills, Python at minimum

• Comfortable working in Linux

• Strong interest in robotics, automation, computer vision, or perception

• English proficiency

• Organized and proactive working style

What we offer 

• 1000 euro monthly compensation

• 10 vacation days during the internship period

• Flexible working hours and the option to work from home 2 days per week where practical

• A direct and significant influence on highly innovative products

• The opportunity to work close to the hardware and the product, with fast iteration and tight feedback loops

• Full ownership of a self-contained system that the rest of the company will depend on

• A team environment where practical experimentation, learning, and ownership are expected

The application procedure 

• If after reading the above you are convinced you are the right person for the job, send us some information about yourself. This can be a resume, website, portfolio, or any other source that gives us a clear impression of your background, technical skills, and hands-on experience.

• We will get back to you ASAP. If we think you could be a fit for the position, we will invite you for an informal introduction so we can get to know you, and equally important, you can get to know us. After this, a more technically focused interview may follow.

• If at that point we believe you are the person we are looking for, we will discuss the specifics such as starting date and internship period.

Welcome to the team!

title: AI Engineer Trainee
description:
Gestalten Sie den digitalen Wandel mit uns

Wir sind konstant auf der Suche nach Menschen, die Veränderungen vorantreiben und die Welt von morgen mitgestalten wollen. Gemeinsam mit unseren Kunden möchten wir wachsen und neue digitale Wege beschreiten. StackWorks macht als zertifizierter Partner von Google und Microsoft die IT von Schweizer KMU einfacher, sicherer und automatisierter.

Ihre Rolle

- Sie bauen die StackWorks-Kompetenz in Automation, AI und Agentics auf und entwickeln sie weiter.

- Sie entwickeln, integrieren und betreiben AI Agents, die Geschäftsprozesse automatisieren, plattformübergreifend auf Google Gemini Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot Studio und Microsoft Foundry sowie vergleichbaren Agent-Plattformen.

- Sie sind technische Sparringinstanz für unsere Cloud Consultants in Pre-Sales und Projekten.

Ihre Aufgaben

- Konzipieren, Entwickeln und Testen von AI Agents für interne und kundenseitige Use Cases in Collaboration, Operations, Sales und Finance

- Anbinden von Agents an Quell- und Zielsysteme über APIs und MCP-Schnittstellen (Create, Read, Update, Delete)

- Ableiten konkreter Use Cases aus Geschäftsprozessen und Übersetzen in Agent-Architekturen

- Auswahl, Bewertung und produktiver Einsatz der relevanten Agent-Plattformen (Google Gemini Enterprise und Vertex AI Agents, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry und weitere)

- Aufsetzen von Guard Rails, Monitoring, Logging und Cost Controls für produktive Agents

- Erstellen technischer Dokumentation, Architekturskizzen und reproduzierbarer Patterns als interne Agent Building Blocks

- Technische Unterstützung der Cloud Consultants in Pre-Sales und Delivery (Machbarkeitsabklärungen, Demos, Prototypen)

- Aufbau und Pflege eines internen Agent-Portfolios als Referenz- und Lernumgebung

- Beobachten der Marktentwicklung im Bereich Agentics und Einbringen relevanter Innovationen

Ihr Profil

- Laufendes oder abgeschlossenes Studium in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder vergleichbar (BSc oder MSc)

- Solide Programmierkenntnisse, idealerweise Python und/oder JavaScript bzw. TypeScript

- Verständnis für moderne AI-Konzepte: LLMs, Prompting, Tool Use, MCP, Agent-Architekturen

- Affinität zu Cloud-Plattformen und APIs (Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure)

- Strukturierte, analytische Arbeitsweise mit ausgeprägter Problemlösekompetenz

- Selbständigkeit und Lernbereitschaft in einem dynamischen Technologiefeld

- Sicheres Auftreten gegenüber Consultants und Kunden, klare schriftliche und mündliche Kommunikation (Deutsch verhandlungssicher, Englisch sehr gut)

- Erste praktische Erfahrungen mit Agent-Plattformen (Google Gemini Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, LangChain o. ä.) sind ein Plus

- Sie streben die Google Cloud Digital Leader Zertifizierung sowie relevante Professional-Zertifizierungen an

Ihre Schnittstellen

- Cloud Consultants und Cloud Engineers: Use-Case-Diskussion, technische Umsetzung, Pre-Sales-Support

- Head of Cloud Engineering (CTO): Architektur, Standards, Technology Choice

- Managing Director: Strategie und Portfolio-Entwicklung im Bereich Automation und AI

Ihre Entwicklung

Der Weg ist klar vorgezeichnet: vom Trainee über Junior AI Engineer und AI Engineer bis zum Senior AI Engineer.

Benefits

- Hybrid Work: Die Hälfte Ihrer Arbeitszeit im Homeoffice, die andere Hälfte mit dem Team im Büro in St. Gallen.

- Work hard, play hard: Gemeinsam gehen wir ins Workout, um den Kopf zu befreien und den Körper in Schwung zu bringen. Wir beteiligen uns an Ihrem Fitness-Abo.

- Learn & Grow: Ein Kontingent für Workshops, Schulungen, Zertifizierungen und externe Kurse.

- A heart for birthday: Lassen Sie sich feiern! Dieser eine, besondere Tag im Jahr gehört nur Ihnen und Sie haben frei.

- Cold Refresh: Unser Kühlschrank ist immer gefüllt mit Getränken, dazu frischer Kaffee aus der Rocket-Maschine.

- Experience true adventures: Regelmässige Events und Teamlunches schweissen uns zusammen und erweitern unseren Horizont.

So geht es weiter

Senden Sie uns Ihre Unterlagen direkt hier über JOIN. Ishan Don meldet sich persönlich bei Ihnen.

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Who is Tenable? 

Tenable® is the Exposure Management company. Over 40,000 organizations around the globe rely on Tenable to understand and reduce cyber risk. Our global employees support 65 percent of the Fortune 500, 50 percent of the Global 2000, and large government agencies. Come be part of our journey!

- Fullstack engineering capabilities with a strong backend foundation.

- Experience working with high-volume data systems.

title: Service Desk L3 - IT Operations Technical Lead
description:
About Nebius: 

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

#LI-IV1 

The role 

The Service Desk IT Operations Lead is the senior individual contributor on the Service Desk path and the senior technical escalation point for Service Desk across EMEA and APAC . The role owns and improves Service Desk processes, runbooks, escalation paths, the employee hardware lifecycle and new-hire IT onboarding, administers Service Desk tooling on behalf of its owners, and leads improvement initiatives and cross-functional projects. It acts as the bridge between the Service Desk and Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications and Security, and leads through expertise, judgment and influence rather than formal authority. It carries no line-management responsibility.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- 
Serve as the final technical escalation point within Service Desk for high-severity, high-complexity and business-critical issues, before engagement of Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications, Security or vendors; coordinate major-incident response, communication and post-incident follow-through with the relevant teams.

- 
Act as consultation point for L1/L2 on complex or unusual cases: advise on troubleshooting approach, ownership, escalation path and resolution before issues are escalated.

- 
Act as subject matter expert for the end-user computing environment: endpoints (Windows, macOS), mobile devices, identity and access (Entra ID / Active Directory, SSO , MFA ), Microsoft 365, MDM , collaboration tools and meeting-room technology.

- 
Administer and configure Service Desk tooling (e.g. Jira Service Management workflows and automation, device enrolment and MDM policy, hardware asset management tooling) as agreed with the tool and platform owners, and propose and implement improvements, including request workflows and automations used by adjacent functions. Ownership of the tools and platforms sits with IT leadership and platform owners.

- 
Administer selected corporate IT systems and services according to operational requirements, including access and permissions management, service configuration and automation.

- 
Maintain and improve Service Desk procedures, runbooks, escalation paths and knowledge base; propose technical standards for approval by Service Desk management and maintain them once approved; advise on operational priorities.

- 
Contribute to creating and updating documentation: runbooks, process documents, technical standards and knowledge-base articles, setting the standard for documentation quality across the team.

- 
Analyze ticket, escalation and SLA data to identify systemic issues and contribute to SLA reporting; lead root-cause analysis and problem management; design process, tooling and automation changes that improve first-time resolution and reduce escalation volume.

- 
Assess proposed solutions and operational changes for supportability and user impact; advise management and partner teams on the support implications of technology decisions.

- 
Provide organizational context on existing and legacy IT processes, systems, decisions and ownership structures; apply it when evaluating current processes, and improve legacy practices where appropriate.

- 
Identify gaps or ambiguities in operational ownership and work with the relevant stakeholders to establish practical solutions.

- 
Own and improve employee-lifecycle processes, including hardware provisioning and, with Onboarding and People teams, new-hire IT onboarding across EMEA and APAC .

- 
Recommend standards for company-provided laptops, peripherals and other end-user equipment, balancing business need, supportability, lifecycle and market availability; maintain the approved standards.

- 
Own employee hardware lifecycle processes, provisioning, replacement, reuse, return, disposal and employee resale, and provide demand forecasts and regional requirements (including Bill & Hold) to IT Supply Chain and Procurement; recommend routine purchases against agreed standards, approving only within a documented delegated spend limit.

- 
Lead and continuously improve equipment reuse and employee resale, including TechShop.

- 
Contribute to forecasting and budget planning for employee technology and Service Desk requirements.

- 
Support Service Desk contracts, renewals and licensing; maintain working relationships with hardware and Service Desk vendors.

- 
Lead Service Desk projects, system migrations, new technology rollouts, process optimization, and contribute Service Desk expertise to company initiatives such as regional expansion, office launches, organizational changes and onboarding improvements, working with Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications, Security, HR/People, Onboarding, Recruiting, Procurement, Workplace/Facilities and the AV /Builds team.

- 
Advise partner functions on Service Desk capabilities, procedures, requirements and dependencies, and work with them to define and improve shared operational processes (e.g. joiner/mover/leaver with People, office launches with Workplace).

- 
Act as technical interviewer in Service Desk recruitment, providing structured feedback and hiring recommendations to management, and technical input to role requirements.

- 
Deliver technical onboarding for new team members and mentor L1 and L2 through joint troubleshooting, coaching and knowledge transfer, documenting approaches to reduce reliance on individual knowledge.

- 
Stay hands-on: support the IT Bar, queue and events alongside L1/L2 when needed, and lead by example on ticket quality and communication.

- 
Provide operational evidence for audits and compliance (including equipment lifecycle and offboarding); follow security, access-governance and procurement requirements; escalate material concerns to the appropriate owner.

We expect you to have: 

- 
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology or related field, or equivalent experience.

- 
5+ years of IT support or service desk experience with demonstrated progression in responsibility.

- 
Advanced technical certifications (Microsoft 365, Azure, ITIL Intermediate, Security+, etc.) strongly preferred.

- 
Deep knowledge of enterprise IT systems, networks, and security practices.

- 
Strong leadership, coaching, and collaboration skills.

- 
Proven ability to manage high-priority incidents and lead cross-functional troubleshooting efforts.

Related Competencies 

- 
Knowledge & Skills 

- 
Recognised expert in end-user computing and support operations, with breadth across endpoints, identity, collaboration, device management and security touch points.

Diagnoses ambiguous, cross-platform issues; experienced in root-cause analysis and process optimisation.

Translates complex issues into clear guidance for technical and non-technical audiences.

- 
Autonomy 

- 
Operates with a high degree of independence and trusted judgment.

Takes the most sensitive escalations from intake to follow-up.

Independently identifies improvements and drives them to completion; proactively pitches projects within the Service Desk domain.

Advises management and partner teams on the support implications of technology decisions. Significant spend, strategic or organisational changes, and decisions outside delegated authority are aligned with management.

- 
Complexity 

- 
Handles the most complex technical and operational problems in the support function: multiple systems, conflicting signals, incomplete data, elevated business risk.

Leads escalations, often coordinating multiple IT functions.

Designs and improves workflows and procedures where no precedent exists.

- 
Impact 

- 
Broad impact on service reliability, SLA performance, support maturity and user experience across EMEA and APAC .

Reduces downtime, repeat incidents and escalation volume.

Shapes employee technology from onboarding through equipment return; ensures knowledge transfer and team readiness.

- 
People / Leadership 

- 
Leads through expertise, coordination and example, not formal authority.

Escalation point and mentor for L1 and L2; shapes team capability over time. Technical interviewer.

No line management: hiring decisions, performance, compensation and other people-management accountabilities sit with Service Desk management.

Benefits & Perks: 

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius: 

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI 

Equal Opportunity Statement: 

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire.

title: Cloud Engineer Automation
description:
Working for a company like Smile Digital Health means supporting our mandate for #BetterGlobalHealth . We strive towards this goal every day, and the results can be seen in the impact of our innovative health data platform and data management solutions, which are used in over 20 countries. We were #19 on Deloitte's Technology Fast 50 Ranking for 2024! 

Smile Digital Health makes it easy for healthcare stakeholders to collect and exchange data with our leading FHIR-based data liberation platform.

At its heart, the Smile platform enables people and organizations to better manage healthcare data. We help generate and liberate structured healthcare data to ensure effective delivery across care teams and health systems bringing #BetterGlobalHealth to patients everyday! 

Apply today and find plenty of reasons to SMILE! 

The Cloud Engineer (Automation) is responsible for designing, building, operating and improving production-grade automation for Smile Digital Health, its clients and partners. This role will be responsible for the pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and recovery procedures, that the platform runs on. 

This Engineer will merge direct platform engineering expertise with driving strategic changes in how the department designs, deploys, and maintains its infrastructure. Key responsibilities include managing build and release engineering, orchestrating the Terraform and Helm infrastructure, provisioning on-demand environments, and implementing automated recovery. This role works closely with Platform Engineering, Solution Engineering, Service Operations and Engineering Practice & QA to remove unnecessary repetitive, manual work and effectively optimize a build from the time the client commits to a running environment faster, decrease platform costs, and utilize AI to enhance the platformâs engineering and operations.

\n 

Responsibilities: 

- Own build and release engineering by reviewing the current repositories and CI setup, then consolidate duplicated Azure DevOps pipeline YAML onto shared reusable templates with change detection and automated quality gates.

- Identify and eliminate manual efforts for cross-functional teams and replace them with scheduled, auditable automation. For example, automating patching, certificate and secret rotation, environment scaling, and recurring reports

- Implement GitOps-based continuous delivery - declarative, Git-driven deployments with automated reconciliation, drift detection and rollback.

- Automate line-of-business environments end to end, provisioned and torn down on demand across every Azure service and application involved.

- Automate business continuity and disaster recovery through backup validation, restore and failover, recurring DR drills, and measured RTO and RPO.

- Ensure Helm and Terraform are easy to upgrade by charting reuse and configuration validation, versioned modules, and state boundaries that limit how far an upgrade reaches.

- Run in-cluster platform services deployed through Helm, harden workloads for availability and capacity: health probes, replica counts, and right-sized requests, limits and autoscaling.

- Ensure that the Terraform configuration is regularly maintained.

- Build and maintain Build Agent images for streamlining tooling available for the builds. 

- Automate the guardrails such as policy-as-code, security and IaC scanning in the pipeline, and alerts and dashboards defined as code.

- Implement AI-assisted engineering in the platform teamâs day-to-day work

- Contribute to the departmentâs AI enablement, package knowledge into reusable skills and runbooks in the shared skill library.

- Work with the development and operations teams to find automation gaps, prioritize them, and close them.

- Troubleshoot production and staging issues and document what you automate so others can operate it.

Requirements: 

- 6+ years of hands-on cloud engineering, DevOps and/or platform engineering experience, including at least 1-2+ years with infrastructure as code and CI/CD automation on Microsoft Azure in production.

- Post-secondary education in Computer Science, Engineering, or similar and/or equivalent work experience. 

- Practical in-depth knowledge and expertise in Terraform, Helm and Azure DevOps pipelines, and GitOps delivery (Argo CD or Flux). 

- Strong Terraform skills including, but not limited to, experience with module design, provider version management, state management and refactoring.

- Expertise in Helm chart authoring and refactoring, including recent experience with Kubernetes and AKS.

- Demonstrated knowledge across Azure (AKS, Key Vault, Storage, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, networking, identity) and observability as code (Azure Monitor and/or Grafana, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry).

- Hands-on experience automating backup, restore and failover with measured RTO and RPO.

- Hands-on experience with agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent), keeping confidential data out of them and reviewing what they produce.

- Hands-on experience running, hardening and right-sizing production workloads on Kubernetes

- Hands-on Kafka operations: topic and partition design, consumer group sizing, and throughput and latency trade-offs. Experience migrating between Kafka platforms (HDInsight, Confluent, MSK or self-managed) is a strong asset.

- Strong Python and Bash skills, able to build maintainable tooling, not glue scripts.

- A demonstrable record of replacing manual processes with automation.

- FinOps practice and Azure Cost Management, an asset. 

- Regulated environment experience (healthcare, PHI), an asset. 

- Certifications: HashiCorp Terraform Associate; Microsoft AZ-104, AZ-400, AZ-305; CKA or CKAD, an asset. 

- Observability as code with Azure Monitor, Grafana, Prometheus, or OpenTelemetry; Azure cost optimization, an asset. 

\n $120,000 - $140,000 a year

\n 

Smile discloses that artificial intelligence (AI) may be used in portions of the recruitment and selection process, such as resume screening or application assessment. All hiring decisions are ultimately made by qualified human decision-makers, and AI tools are used to support â not replace â fair and equitable hiring practices. 

This position is a new role, created to support Smileâs continued growth and commitment to operational excellence.

Some of the benefits we offer:

Smile's core values include respect, inclusion, embracing our differences, and celebrating shared values because our people are the foundation of our success. title: Senior Applied Scientist
description:
Meet the team 

You’ll join the Traffic Control Features team within TomTom’s Automated Driving organization . The team builds the technology that turns real-world observations into reliable map information about traffic signs, traffic lights, stop lines and road markings . 

You’ll work with applied scientists and software engineers to develop algorithms and machine-learning solutions that detect, position and connect these features to the right roads and driving directions. The goal is to deliver accurate, scalable map content that supports navigation and advanced driving experiences. TomTom measures these features using quality dimensions such as recall, precision, and road-relation accuracy. 

What you will do: 

- Develop algorithms and ML solutions for traffic signs, traffic lights, road markings, and other traffic-control features, including projects with Computer Vision and Image Recognition. 

- Design and productionize solutions that extract reliable map information from diverse, large-scale and noisy real-world data sources, including car sensor data and unstructured information. 

- Improve how features are detected, positioned, and associated with the correct road/lane and driving direction. 

- Drive measurable improvements in recall, precision, and overall map quality against customer-facing targets. 

- Own components of production pipelines, from input data and feature extraction through evaluation and validated map output. 

- Solve complex problems involving geospatial geometry, map matching, computer vision, image recognition, noisy observations, ground-truth quality, and large-scale evaluation. 

- Run experiments, translate successful approaches into production solutions, and clearly document outcomes. 

- Use AI tools, such as Claude Code, to support problem solving, data analysis, implementation, and engineering productivity. 

- Mentor junior colleagues, provide insightful code reviews, and contribute to hiring. 

What you will need: 

- 4+ years of professional experience in Applied Science, Machine Learning, algorithm development, computer vision or related field. 

- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Geospatial Science, Statistics or another quantitative field. Master’s or PhD is a plus. 

- Strong fundamentals in algorithms and machine learning , including model development, evaluation, statistics and experimental design. 

- Proficiency in Python , an ML framework such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, and large-scale data processing tools such as Spark or Databricks. 

- Experience taking algorithms, ML models or data pipelines from experimentation into production . 

- Experience leading well-scoped technical projects and mentoring junior colleagues. 

- Ability to work across data, algorithms, modeling, ground truth and evaluation rather than operating within only one area of expertise. 

- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to independently approach complex and ambiguous problems. 

- Proficient written and verbal communication skills in English. 

- You already live in the Netherlands. We cannot offer relocation for this role. 

What we offer 

A competitive compensation package, of course. 

Time and resources to grow and develop, including a personal development budget and paid leave for learning days, as well as paid access to e-learning resources such as O’Reilly and LinkedIn Learning. 

Time to support life outside of work, with enhanced parental leave plus paid leave to care for loved ones and volunteer in local communities. 

Work flexibility, where TomTom’ers, in agreement with their manager and team, use both the office and home to focus, collaborate, learn and socialize. It’s all about getting the best out of both worlds – we ask TomTom’ers to come to the office two days a week, and the remaining three are free to be worked in either location.

Improve your home office with a setup budget and get extra support with a monthly allowance. 

Enjoy options to work from your home country and abroad for a set number of days each year, to visit family and friends, or to simply explore the world we’re mapping. 

Take the holidays you want with a competitive holiday plan, plus an extra day off to celebrate your birthday. 

Join annual events like our Hackathon and DevDays to bring your ideas to life with talented teammates from around the world. 

Become a part of our inclusive global culture and have the chance to collaborate with a diverse community – we have over 80 nationalities at TomTom! 

Find out more about our global benefits and enjoy additional local benefits tailored to your location. 

Meet your team 

We’re Maps, a global team within TomTom’s Location Technology Products technical unit. Our team is driven to deliver the most up-to-date, accurate and detailed maps for hundreds of millions of users around the world. Joining our team, you’ll continuously innovate our mapmaking processes, directly contributing to our vision: engineering the world's most trusted and useful map.

At TomTom... 

You’ll help people find their way in the world. In 2004, TomTom revolutionized how the world moves with the introduction of the first portable navigation device. Now, we intend to do it again by engineering the first-ever real-time map, the smartest and most useful map on the planet.

Work with a team of 3,300+ unique, curious and passionate problem-solvers. Together, we’ll open up a world of possibilities for car manufacturers, enterprises and developers to help people understand and get closer to the world around them.

After you apply 

Our recruitment team will work hard to give you a meaningful experience throughout your journey with us, no matter the outcome. Your application will be screened closely and you can rest assured that all follow-up actions will be thorough, from assessments and interviews all the way through onboarding. To find out more about our application process, check out our hiring FAQs .

TomTom is an equal opportunity employer 

TomTom is where you can find your place in the world. Every day we welcome, nurture and celebrate differences. Why? Because your uniqueness is what makes you, you . No matter your culture or background, you’ll find your impact at TomTom. Research also shows that sometimes women and underrepresented communities can be hesitant to apply for positions unless they believe they meet 100% of the criteria. If you can relate to this, please know that we’d love to hear from you.

title: System Identification Engineer
description:
About Us 

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the role 

Every airframe Harmattan AI flies starts with a model. System identification turns flight data into the verified dynamics that guidance and control are designed, tuned and trained on. It is the foundation of an autopilot that adapts across multirotors, fixed wings, VTOLs and missiles.

As a System Identification Engineer, working out of Lausanne, you will own the path from flight test to identified model. You will design and run your own experiments, build a repeatable identification pipeline, and deliver models the G&C team can trust.

Responsibilities 

- Experiment Design & Flight Test: Plan and run your own identification tests, from excitation design to flight tests, including coordinating with the .

- Model Identification: Identify rigid-body, aerodynamic, propulsion and actuator dynamics using frequency and time-domain methods, including closed-loop identification on vehicles flown under a controller.

- Propulsion & Actuators: Characterize motors, ESCs, propellers and control surfaces, including bandwidth, delays, saturation, and thermal and battery effects.

- Identification Pipeline: Build and maintain an automated, reproducible pipeline from flight logs to identified model. This covers ingestion, data-quality checks, estimation, validation and reporting.

- Model Validation: Validate models against held-out flight data, quantify uncertainty, and make sure each model is fit for purpose: controller design, simulation, or training learned G&C.

- New Airframes: Extend the capability from multirotors to control-surface multirotors, fixed wings, tail-sitters and missiles.

- Simulation & G&C Support: Deliver models into simulation, SITL and HITL, and work closely with control, guidance and embedded engineers to close the loop between models and flight results.

- Mentorship: Depending on seniority, support the team by mentoring junior engineers and interns.

Candidate Requirements 

- Educational Background: A strong academic record with a degree in aerospace, control, mechanical engineering or a related STEM field. A practical track record matters more than the specific degree.

- System Identification: Proven experience identifying dynamic models of flying platforms from real data, in both the frequency and time domain, including the pitfalls of closed-loop data.

- Flight Mechanics & Control: Solid grasp of rigid-body dynamics, aerodynamic forces and moments, non-dimensionalization, stability modes and propulsion models. Also enough control background to know what the model will be used for.

- Flight Testing: Hands-on experience planning and running flight tests and working from raw, imperfect logs.

- Software: Strong Python and scientific computing skills, with the discipline to build tools others can rerun.

Nice to have 

- Rigorous about data quality, uncertainty and validation; skeptical of models until they are proven.

- Autonomous and hands-on, comfortable moving between bench, field and code.

- Communicates clearly, able to present models and test results to engineers and senior stakeholders.

- Thrives under pressure in a fast-paced environment with a no-task-is-too-small mentality.

- Fixed-wing aerodynamic modeling; VTOL or tail-sitter dynamics; remote pilot certification; experience with real flight logs; structural or vibration modes; data-driven or learned dynamics models.

- Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI’s mission of providing a defensive edge to allied nations through ethical, high-impact technology.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Staff Applied AI Researcher (Agentic Search)
description:
We are seeking a Staff Applied AI Researcher to join a fast-growing team building an agent-native search platform - the web access layer for AI systems.

You can think of this as Google search, but for AI agents: a system designed for machines, not humans. We are building agentic search, where AI systems actively plan, retrieve, evaluate, and refine information rather than simply returning results. As AI becomes the primary interface to the web, this layer will replace the role of traditional search engines.

We are designing these systems to search and reason over web data in real time, under strict latency and reliability constraints. This means solving retrieval, ranking and passage extraction under entirely new access patterns and at significant scale, with systems operating over constantly changing, unstructured data and serving tens of thousands of production workloads 24/7.

This role comes with ownership over key parts of our applied AI research direction and system design, with a strong expectation of defining new approaches and shipping measurable impact in production. In the first year, you will own a specific part of the search stack, e.g. ranking or iterative retrieval.

What you'll work on: 

- 
Designing an agent-native search system that handles everything from low-latency single-hop search to complex deep search tasks requiring iterative planning, querying, refinement and reasoning.

- 
Training ranking and retrieval models optimized for agent-driven workflows under real world constraints

- 
Bringing the latest advances from the research community to our search stack and ship it to production.

Your responsibilities: 

- 
Drive applied research and technical direction across retrieval and ranking systems

- 
Design and evolve multi-stage retrieval architectures (query understanding, rewriting, retrieval, reranking and iterative retrieval)

- 
Lead experimentation on modern retrieval approaches (embedding research, sparse and hybrid retrieval, reranking, context compression) and bring them into production

- 
Develop methods for grounding LLMs in real-time web data at scale, using trust, quality and freshness signals to surface reliable sources

- 
Partner with the evaluation team to define new metrics for agentic systems, where correctness is not reducible to clicks

- 
Analyze trade-offs across relevance, latency, and cost, and work closely with engineering to deploy systems that operate at web scale

- 
Mentor researchers and engineers and help raise the technical bar of the team

Must haves: 

- 
8+ years of experience in applied AI, ML, or software engineering

- 
Proven track record of shipping ML or AI systems to production at scale

- 
Deep experience with search, retrieval, ranking or building RAG-based assistants

- 
Strong understanding of modern deep learning, especially transformers and embeddings

- 
Experience with LLM-integrated or knowledge-intensive systems

- 
Experience designing evaluation frameworks and metrics for ML systems

- 
Strong programming skills in Python

- 
Top-tier publications ( ICLR , ICML , NeurIPS, AAAI , EMNLP , ACL )

- 
Ability to operate in a fast-moving, product-driven environment with high ownership and autonomy

Nice to haves 

- 
Background in agentic AI systems (agents, tool use, autonomous workflows)

- 
Experience with RL post-training of LLMs or VLMs

description:
Cardog | Toronto, Canada or REMOTE | Full-time
https://cardog.app/careers We're the system of record for the Canadian vehicle: raw automotive data turned into facts that can be checked. Our open-source VIN decoder sits underneath a government vehicle registry. Some of what's interesting: - A government registry, a manufacturer's own filing, a listing site and an insurance record will describe the same truck four different ways, and nothing in any of those files says they're the same truck. Reconciling that, for every vehicle in the country, in a way that holds up when a regulator asks how you know, is most of the data work. - Seventeen characters on a door frame encode manufacturer, plant, model year and build attributes — badly, inconsistently, and differently per manufacturer. Public reference data covers some of it. The rest gets worked out from filings, recall documents, and patterns inferred across millions of vehicles. - We read vehicles directly over OBD-II now. Forty modules answered on a recent Hyundai, each reporting its own part number and installed software version. Nothing downstream of the VIN moves when a module is reflashed, so no registration, history report or dealer system knows what software is actually in a car. The platform connects providers, patients, payers, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical companies in real time. You will design systems built for high load, with self healing, auto scaling, and full observability.

You bring strong judgment about AI. You know when AI speeds up delivery and when AI produces weak code. You apply AI to raise code quality, performance, and design standards across the team, and you solve real problems for the pharmacies and prescribers who rely on our platform.

This team owns critical parts of the case execution workflow, including eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These systems sit at the operational core of how Pivotal delivers outcomes for providers.

This is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex, workflow-driven backend problems and working through data-heavy decision logic. Who You Are 

- 5+ years of software engineering experience with a strong backend focus

- Strong engineering fundamentals with hands-on experience building data-heavy, workflow-oriented systems

- Experience working on complex, data-driven decision logic or orchestration problems: you're comfortable with systems where correctness and sequencing both matter

- Self-directed and proactive: you identify problems and drive them to resolution without heavy oversight

Not a full-time seat. Engagement: Ongoing 1099 contract. Milestone prices are set against a frozen spec. This is not a full-time seat. First package: A fixed-price flows-and-kit package, about three weeks. After that, $50–75/hr as each product grows. Location: SF Bay Area, hybrid, with in-person working sessions for kickoff and reviews. Start: Immediately after selection. Level: Mid-level welcome. You work directly with the founding CTO. Early sessions are for breaking the product down together. After that, scope is deliverable by deliverable. ABOUT THE STUDIO:
We are a small Bay Area product studio. Several products, one stack, one visual language. You own the UX with us: who the user is, what they are trying to finish, what belongs on each screen, and what happens when it fails. Later products reuse the same tokens, components, and patterns so customers and our engineers are not learning a new UI every time. The products are B2B web apps: dashboards, media and content libraries, status views, and auth and access-gate states. The first product in the queue is a digital signage CMS. Store owners upload content, build playlists, pair outdoor Android screens from a phone, and see what is playing. The app is a mobile-first PWA. The screen on the sidewalk has its own states: setup QR, downloading, no content, and error. You take a real part in that breakdown. Bring a point of view on structure, priority, and what to cut. Sit with us and map the flows before the high-fidelity screens exist. When a familiar admin layout is the wrong job for the task, say so and show the alternative. The screens still have to ship. We start from a Tailwind UI / shadcn component kit. Buttons, inputs, tables, cards, and dialogs stay that anatomy, restyled with our brand: color, type, radius, and density. Page structure, hierarchy, and flow are yours. Every screen is composed from those components, with tokens that map to our Tailwind theme, so the frontend team builds from the system. FOR MORE DETAILS OR TO APPLY: https://vuetech.sh/careers

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote

URL: https://www.samsara.com/ 

About the role: 

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world. The platform processes 25+ trillion data points annually from IoT sensors, cameras, and connected devices across thousands of organizations, and that dataset is compounding: it grew from 4 trillion to 25+ trillion in four years. We're still early in turning that data into the products that will define how physical operations run, and we're hiring the engineers who will build what comes next.

We're approaching ~$2B ARR growing 30%+ year over year, with 96% of our largest customers on two or more products. The fastest-growing divisions at Samsara are tackling the hardest, most ambiguous problems at the company: building new products from scratch, applying AI and ML to massive real-world datasets, and shipping capabilities that change how organizations maintain equipment, manage fleets, and run day-to-day operations. Most of this work is zero-to-one, at billion-dollar scale.

We're looking for software engineers who want to define what ships next. Leveling is broad and flexible: we're hiring from Senior through Staff+, across platform and product, and we're open to shaping scope around the right person's strengths and interests. That window won't stay open long.

This role is remote and open to candidates residing in the US. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role. 

You should apply if: 

- You want to impact the industries that run our world. The software you build will have real-world stakes: helping keep the lights on, getting food into grocery stores, keeping workers safe. What ships here isn't metrics on a dashboard. It shows up on the loading dock, the job site, and the dispatch floor.

- You want to build, not maintain. Samsara is in full growth mode. We're building new systems from scratch, not babysitting old ones. You'd own entire problem spaces end to end, with the autonomy to set direction from day one.

- You want to work where AI meets the physical world. Samsara has spent a decade building the largest proprietary dataset for physical operations. More connected assets generate more data, more data trains better models, better models drive more value, and more value wins more assets. The market and the opportunity here are what set us apart, not just the models.

- You believe customers are more than a number. Samsara engineers have a rare closeness to end users. You'll participate in customer interviews, collaborate with product managers and customer success, and use that context to build products that solve real problems operators face every day.

- You have the curiosity and drive to figure it out. We're looking for people who take pride in their work and get things done at all costs. The engineers who thrive here don't wait to be told what to build. They define it, ship it, and own the outcome. The rate-limiting step on our teams isn't tooling or process. It's ambition.

In this role, you will: 

- Take ownership of technically complex, mission-critical areas and run with them. We want to point you in a direction and show up to the demo meeting impressed, not spend our weeks managing the details.

- Define and drive technical strategy for new products and platform capabilities, from backend services and APIs to the customer-facing UI.

- Design and ship full-stack features end to end. You'll work across backend, frontend, and potentially mobile to deliver AI-powered products that solve real operational problems.

- Partner with product, design, and customer-facing teams to translate ambiguous, real-world problems into clear technical plans and measurable outcomes.

- Build and scale the systems behind AI-driven products, including data ingestion, APIs, and the workflows that put intelligence into the hands of operators.

- Raise the bar for the engineers around you through code reviews, design reviews, technical mentorship, and by setting a standard for quality, velocity, and craft.

- Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role: 

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

- 8+ years of experience in software design and development, including building and operating production systems at scale.

- Strong full-stack fundamentals. You're comfortable working across backend services, APIs, and frontend (web or mobile) to ship complete products.

- Proficiency in modern languages and frameworks (Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, React, or similar).

- Demonstrated experience leading cross-team or cross-org projects from inception through rollout, including managing ambiguity, driving alignment, and delivering measurable impact.

- Experience building AI-powered or data-driven products. You don't need to train models, but you know how to take AI capabilities and turn them into products customers love.

- Strong communication skills and the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- A track record of building: zero-to-one products, systems you left in a meaningfully better place, or hard problems you refused to let stay unsolved.

An ideal candidate also has: 

- Experience shipping AI-powered features in production, whether that's LLM-based products, agentic workflows, recommendation systems, or other customer-facing AI.

- Comfort with modern AI-augmented development workflows (Cursor, LLMs, etc.) to multiply your output and accelerate delivery.

- Background working with real-world operational data (telematics, sensor data, work orders, inspections) or a strong interest in learning the domain.

- A proven track record of mentoring senior engineers and influencing engineering culture, standards, and best practices beyond a single team.

- Side projects, open-source contributions, or other signals of curiosity and drive outside the scope of your day job.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary

$162,400 — $290,000 USD

Total Rewards 

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara 

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/samsara-staff-software-engineer

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
For this role, we will only consider candidates who are currently based in the Netherlands. 

About SkinVision 

Skin cancer is highly treatable when caught early, but limited access to specialist care and long wait times delay diagnosis, increasing the risk of late-stage cases and driving up treatment costs. SkinVision, founded in Amsterdam in 2012, exists to close that gap. Our proprietary AI — certified as a Class IIa medical device under EU regulation, with over 90% sensitivity and 89% specificity — has already helped nearly 3 million people worldwide detect early signs of skin cancer. Today, SkinVision has a database of more than 6 million skin spot assessments and can reach 20 million people through insurer partnerships. High-risk cases are reviewed by a team of dermatologists, who support users in taking the right next step — from urgent care to a specialist referral. We are extending this further, connecting users faster to the specialist care they need. We're a focused, international team, active globally, united by one goal: making early detection accessible to everyone, everywhere. If you join us, you're not just building a product — you're helping close the gap between a person noticing something and getting the care they need. 

DevOps at SkinVision 

As a DevOps Engineer at SkinVision, you will play a key role in building, scaling, and securing the infrastructure that powers our AI-driven health platform. You’ll design and maintain our cloud-based systems in AWS, implement CI/CD pipelines, enhance observability using Datadog, and drive operational excellence through automation and monitoring. 

Your work will directly impact the reliability and scalability of a medical-grade system that serves users globally. You’ll collaborate closely with backend, ML, and product teams to ensure smooth delivery, rapid deployments, and resilient operations — ultimately enabling us to deliver life-saving technology with confidence. 

Beyond hands-on expertise with AWS and modern DevOps tooling, we’re looking for someone who thinks architecturally. You’ll get to know our current setup, form your own view of how it should evolve, and help define a target vision for our infrastructure, then drive its implementation. Day-to-day operational work is part of the role, but we value someone who thinks before building and takes ownership of where our infrastructure goes next. 

What you will do 

Cloud Infrastructure & Automation 

- Design, build, and manage AWS-based infrastructure, ensuring high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency. 

- Implement and manage infrastructure as code (IaC) using tools like Terraform or CloudFormation. 

- Automate environment provisioning, configuration, and deployments using CI/CD pipelines. 

- Ensure system resilience, security, and performance through automated monitoring and alerting. 

CI/CD & Deployment 

- Design and optimize CI/CD pipelines to support rapid, reliable, and safe deployments across environments. 

- Manage deployment workflows using Argo CD and Kubernetes. 

- Collaborate with developers and ML engineers to streamline build, test, and release processes. 

- Integrate automated testing, rollback strategies, and version control into the deployment lifecycle. 

Observability & Monitoring

About Sodalis

Specialty pharmacy is where the most complex and expensive drugs reach the most in-need patients, and it still runs on faxes, phone tag, and manual data entry. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait.

Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist.

We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx).

Â 

The Opportunity

Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own.
We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live.

We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range.
You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture.

What you'll do

- Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between.

- Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy.

- Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site.

- Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range.

- Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture.

What we're looking for

- 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering.

- You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services.

- You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded.

- You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them.

- You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity.

- You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required.

How we work

We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. It's intense, and it isn't for everyone. We want people who want to build something that matters, alongside others who care as much as they do. If that's you, we should talk.
